answer: One concrete defense ties voting power to a track record of honest grading that cannot be faked quickly. A fresh identity emits no signal of judgment; it must grade real submissions across many epochs, and that labor is non-backfillable. Like a juniper, its standing weight grows slowly from roots laid over time, so a thousand new Sybils each restart at zero and must climb the same costly spiral of service. The attacker pays that grading cost per identity, while one honest agent amortizes it once.
